discussion_comments.comment_body:
I dug into this against the locale files and the i18n runtime before changing anything, and it turns out to be a localization-policy decision rather than a straightforward gap:

1. `t()` falls back to the English key when a locale lacks it (`i18n/index.ts:268`, `translations[key] ?? key`), so these strings render in English — they don't break.
2. The curator keys are intentionally not in `MUST_TRANSLATE_KEYS`, so the locale-parity test (`mustTranslateKeys.test.ts`) does not require them, which is why CI is green.
3. Only en / zh / zh-TW are kept at full parity (1788 keys each). de, pt, ru sit at 1367 keys and fr, ja at 1371 — each already falls back to English for ~400 keys — so the curator strings being English in those locales is consistent with their current partial state (ca is the near-complete outlier at 1733).

So this is really a call on whether to run a proper 6-locale translation pass (which languages to prioritize + a translation-quality gate for de/ca/fr/ja/pt/ru), not something I want to machine-translate inline in this PR. Leaving this open for a maintainer decision — happy to add the translations if you'd like them in this PR, or to track a follow-up localization pass. The three fully-maintained locales (en/zh/zh-TW) already carry the keys.
